title: Helen Haines updates: PM says person in custody after alleged attack on Helen Haines; police say she is in critical condition
summary:
Independent MP injured in an incident involving a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, in regional Victoria. Follow updates

‘No ongoing threat to community’: Victoria…

blocks.text: Victorian police release statement
Victorian police have released a statement, and said they have arrested a man who allegedly struck a women with a vehicle in Wangaratta.
Police say the woman – known to be Haines – is in hospital with “critical injuries”.
Police allege it was a white Toyota Landcruiser that struck Haines on Murphy Street at about 3.35pm, and that there was a knife seized from inside the vehicle.
The statement says:

double quotation markWhen he exited the Toyota, the driver, a 43-year-old Tarrawingee man, was arrested at the scene by a passerby. He will be interviewed in relation to the incident. The woman was taken to hospital with critical injuries. A knife was located by police and seized from inside the Toyota. At this stage, police are investigating as to whether this was an intentional act. It is not known yet if the parties are known to each other. Major Collision Investigation Unit detectives are en route. The investigation remains ongoing.

blocks.text: Acting Superintendent, Ashley Mason, says he was “not aware” of any prior concerns or incidents related to Helen Haines before today’s incident.
Asked how long the area will remain a crime scene, he says:

double quotation markWe’ve got our investigators from the Major Collision Investigation Unit who are currently en route to Wangaratta from Melbourne. So they’ve got significant travel time as well as the time it will take for them to thoroughly process the crime scene once they arrive. I think. There’s some talk that there might be specialist terrorist related police involved in the investigation. We’ve notified our crime and counter–terrorism command and they’re currently liaison and assisting our investigators.
‘No ongoing threat to community’: Victoria police
Mason tells journalists there is “nothing to indicate at this stage” that the two parties are known to each other, but police are still investigating.
He says there is no ongoing or further threat to the community or any other individual at this stage.

double quotation markI can provide some assurance to the community that we certainly do not have any intelligence that there is any further or ongoing threat to any other person or the broader community. We are treating this as an isolated incident at this point in time.
Acting Supt Ashley Mason is addressing the media in Wangaratta.
He says police are still investigating whether the incident was targeted.

double quotation markWe’ve still got a lot to work through here. As you can imagine, it’s been quite dynamic this afternoon. We’ve got quite an extensive crime scene. We have investigators present and they’ll continue to work through and try and collect all available evidence to ascertain exactly what has occurred and how it has occurred. We’ve got the Major Collision Investigation Unit who are currently en route from Melbourne.
Mason also will not confirm whether the incident was politically motivated.
Albanese is asked whether the government knew about any threats made towards Helen Haines.
Albanese says broadly, that he has called for the “temperature to be turned down” in political discourse.

double quotation markIt is too early, though, to speculate on motivation, and we won’t be doing so. We’ll allow the authorities to do their work. Obviously, Helen Haines has suffered … this is a serious incident, and so our thoughts are with Helen and her recovery at this time.
He’s also asked about what security measures were in place for Haines ahead of the incidence.
Albanese says security arrangements are made “based upon the threat levels which are there”.

double quotation markAnyone who looks at comments made and directed towards members of parliament and high office holders – there is increased heightened risk has occurred. Our thoughts are just very much with Helen, her family, her community at this time.
He ends the press conference there.
Albanese says his thoughts and his prayers are with Haines, her family and her community.

double quotation markHelen Haines is incredibly hard-working. She is fiercely intelligent, but most importantly, she’s just a thoroughly decent human being, full of integrity and respected right across the parliament, and from everyone who comes into contact with her, she is a well-loved member of her community, and this will come as an incredible shock to that community. Our thoughts remain with Helen Haines at this very difficult time.
The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, says there has been an increase in reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against MPs and their offices in recent years.
double quotation markThe year before last, we had 951 reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against various high office holders. The more recent financial year, that 951 has gone to 1,067.
PM says suspect in custody after alleged attack on Haines
Anthony Albanese is holding a press conference in Sydney, and says there is a major police investigation underway, and that a suspect is in custody.
He says the motive for the alleged attack is not known.

double quotation markThere is a major police investigation underway, and I can confirm that a suspect is in custody. The Australian Federal Police, Victorian Police, and Asio are working together on this. The joint counter-terrorism team has been activated, but the motive is not known.
Nationals frontbencher Michael McCormack, whose electorate shares a border with Haines’ has written on social media:
double quotation markSending my love and best wishes to Helen Haines for a full and speedy recovery. Such awful news.

We’re expecting the prime minister and home affairs minister to speak shortly from Sydney.
Helen Haines' family release statement
Helen Haines’ family have released a statement to the media.
They have thanked bystanders, health workers and the police.

double quotation markThis afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care. We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response. Our family, and Helen’s staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media. Please keep Helen in your thoughts.
Krishani Dhanji
Good evening, Krishani Dhanji with you here. We will be bringing you live coverage of the prime minister’s press conference, after an incident that has left independent MP Helen Haines injured.
The incident took place near her office in Wangaratta in regional Victoria.
Anthony Albanese and the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, will be speaking from Sydney shortly.
